test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

My mother is 51 years old, / and my uncle is 48 years old. / So my mother is old than my uncle.

options.text: and my uncle is 48 years old.
So my mother is old than my uncle.

solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. So my mother is old than my uncle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrase **"So my mother is old than my uncle."**
 
• The correct comparative form of the adjective **'old'** is **'older'**, not **'old.'**
 
• Comparative adjectives are used to compare two entities, and the correct usage in this context is **'older than.'**

Correct sentence: *My mother is 51 years old, and my uncle is 48 years old. So my mother is **older than** my uncle.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Adjectives:**
 
 
• Comparative adjectives are formed by adding **'-er'** to the base adjective (e.g., old → older) or using **'more'** before the adjective (e.g., beautiful → more beautiful).
 
• They are followed by the word **'than'** to indicate the comparison.
 
• **Example:** She is taller than her brother.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• Superlative adjectives are formed by adding **'-est'** to the base adjective (e.g., old → oldest) or using **'most'** before the adjective (e.g., beautiful → most beautiful).
 
• They are used to compare more than two entities.
 
• **Example:** She is the tallest in the class.
 
 

1ba:T1
